Independent term-condition argument and symbolic table check in rationale
correctness.rationale: Independently, testing the term condition on xy with first input 0 versus x and second input 0 versus y forces every xy into the total commutator zero block. Conversely A² is an ideal, and its quotient is a vector space with zero product, so all polynomial differences in one input block are independent of the other block and the term condition holds there. The same xy test forces a central element to annihilate, using also yx; if an input changes by a two-sided annihilator element, expansion by bilinearity kills every changed monomial involving a product at the first product node above that element. The remaining linear difference is independent of the other block, proving centrality. The second center is therefore the inverse image of the quotient annihilator. In the given table b², bc, cb, c² span, and right multiplication by b sends a,b,c to the independent d,a,c and d to 0. Modulo kd the same test kills b and c coefficients only; a,d annihilate the quotient on both sides. In the lower bound C=Ann(A) cannot be zero if the center grows. B=A/C remains perfect and has nonzero annihilator. Multiplication factors through (B/Ann(B))⊗(B/Ann(B)), so for dim B≤2 its image has dimension at most one (zero if dim B=1), contradicting B²=B. The basis tests and dimension argument work unchanged in characteristic two and every other characteristic.
residual_risks: The proof establishes the minimum within the specified single-product signature, not a minimum for all semiassociative Mal’cev algebras or uniqueness of the table.

value.rationale: This resolves a specific natural subclass of the stated unconditional Grün question by locating its first possible failure. The quotient dimension obstruction shows why small examples cannot work; the characteristic-independent product table is a minimal benchmark for testing stronger hypotheses, not just an isolated calculation of a center.
residual_risks: Does not answer the general classification question or classify all minimum witnesses.
